summary: This report covers a full two-week window (Aug 28 - Sep 11); the Sep 4 run crashed before publishing, so nothing in here has ever been delivered to anyone. Across fourteen days the client sent 41 messages and ALTR sent 32 — and not one carried-over commitment was closed. Ollie Mckinlay, the account lead, contributed four messages totalling fourteen words: 'Thank you' (Aug 29), 'Will look into this for you' (Aug 29), 'Thank you very much' (Sep 1) and 'Looking at this for you shortly' (Sep 10). Two of those four are open-ended promises to investigate something, and neither has an outcome posted. Both were triggered by Mayson @-tagging him rather than by the client — the fourth and fifth such escalations since Jul 28. The $2,200 John order is now twenty days delivered-and-unconfirmed: Vale uploaded the $2,000 custom the fan paid for in May on Aug 22, Ollie collected a further $200 for ASAP delivery on Aug 18, and in the twenty days since nobody has told her the fan received any of it. The March-to-date reconciliation that would settle whether fan u490240243 is owed one delivery or two is 24 days old and has not started. The older paid backlog — Ryan $600 (97 days since sale), John's $1,800 videocall (133 days since Fred logged it), Tyler's $700 JOI custom (159 days) — went a fourth consecutive window without a single mention by anyone, including Vale. On billing the picture is worse than last week, not better. She paid the Sep 1 invoice inside four days — 'Hi yes I sent it already' (Sep 5), her tenth on-time payment since March — but Stephski's reply was 'Perf thank you love', an acknowledgement of the claim rather than a verification that the funds landed. That is now two consecutive payments (Aug 17 and Sep 5) sitting unverified against an account number that changed on the Aug 15 invoice, the fourth banking change in five months. The Aug 17 payment is 25 days unacknowledged. The pre-invoice OF-withdrawal reminder was skipped on Aug 29-30 for the first time since May and the next one is due Sep 14. Meanwhile ALTR opened two brand-new workstreams and made two new asks of the client. On Sep 4 Mayson pitched 'a brand new feature for posting trial reels on instagram more effectively' — which Vale had already been doing for two days off Mica's Aug 31 advice ('Okay yeah I just started like 2 days ago lol'), so the pitch arrived after the client had independently executed the plan and nobody internally knew. The Monday call he proposed for Sep 7 was never booked and never happened. On Sep 9-10 he launched a Snapchat posting team, asked for admin access and told her to 'upload as much photos as possible for snapchat'. She answered 'I have my personal and an of one' and 'What’s its for ?' — the second question got an answer, the first never did, so as of the window close she has been asked to hand admin rights over an unspecified Snapchat account. She already gave ALTR her Snapchat handle on Jul 31. Finally, on Sep 10 Vale posted two screenshots into the OnlyFans topic captioned 'Again' and 'And this one'. Mayson escalated with '@olkmck'; Ollie replied 'Looking at this for you shortly' and posted nothing further. The images are not readable from the log, but the format — unlabelled screenshots into the OnlyFans topic with a one-word caption — is exactly how she raised the Jul 17, Aug 1 and Aug 11 chat-team incidents, and the word 'Again' asserts a repeat. Last week's 'third clean fan-trust week' claim can no longer be made with confidence. What is genuinely good: Michelle's leak-removal reports landed on cadence on Sep 1 and Sep 8 with no repeat complaint since Aug 30; Mica's Aug 31 IG diagnosis was strong enough that the client ran the three-variant hook test herself; Vale is 10-for-10 on payments and has never once been the problem on this account.

health.rationale: Down 5 from 52 over a two-week window in which ALTR closed nothing. The first half (Aug 28 - Sep 4) contained the only real ALTR work: Mica's same-evening diagnosis of the Instagram reach collapse and Michelle's twelve-hour leak-surge turnaround. The second half produced one Ollie message, zero Mica messages, one Michelle report, one Stephski nudge, and a burst of new growth asks from Mayson. Every large exposure aged another fortnight: the $2,200 John order is 20 days delivered-unconfirmed, the March-to-date reconciliation 24 days unstarted, the written PPV/private-live rule 30 days, the girl-girl vault purge 40 days, the Infloww unauthorized-access enquiry and her unanswered 'Should I change my password?' 45 days, Mayson's biweekly call 60 days, and roughly $3,100 of paid customs and calls 97 to 159 days. Billing got materially riskier rather than safer: she paid again on Sep 5 and Stephski acknowledged the claim without verifying the landing, so two consecutive payments are now unreconciled against an account number that changed on the Aug 15 invoice, and the withdrawal reminder was missed for the first time since May. Against that, two things hold the score up. The client is still fully engaged and still paying on time — she executed Mica's hook test unprompted and paid the Sep 1 invoice inside four days. And Mayson is visibly trying to add value, even if the trial-reel pitch duplicated work the client had already started and the Monday call he proposed never happened. The score is dragged down rather than off a cliff because nothing new broke on the client's side; it is ALTR's own follow-through and billing hygiene that regressed. Prior scores: 70 (Aug 8), 62 (Aug 14), 60 (Aug 21), 48 (Aug 28), 52 (Sep 4).
